newsitem.title: USA: NovaCare appoints CEO, creates unit.
newsitem.headline: NovaCare appoints CEO, creates unit.

text.p: NovaCare Inc said Wednesday it appointed Loren Hulber as president and chief executive, a newly created position.

Hulber worked before at American Brands, where he was president and chief executive of Day-Timers Inc. At Day-Timers, he reestablished Day-Timers as the number one brand in time management and personal organization, NovaCare said.

In addition, NovaSource, a newly created, wholly owned of subsididary of NovaCare,, said that it has reached an agreement in principle to handle the human resource functions for NovaCare's 16,700 employees.

NovaSource also owns Resource One, a Florida-based professional employer organization that was acquired in October 1996. NovaSource becomes the PEO industry's second largest and fastest growing major participant with annualized revenues of $812 million, 1,550 clients and 35,400 worksite employees.

The acquired companies include Employee Services of America in Bradenton, Fla. with 9,000 worksite employees (subject to regulatory approval); The TPI Group Ltd. of Queensbury, NY with 7,000 worksite employees; and PROSTAFF Human Resources, Inc. of Bradenton, Fla. with 400 worksite employees. Terms of the
transactions were not released, although NovaCare said it made the purchases with a combination of cash and securities of NovaSource.

The company said the growth of NovaSource represents a key development in NovaCare's ongoing strategy to aggressively integrate its occupational health and outpatient rehabilitation networks with full-service healthcare systems in 10 to 15 selected markets. NovaSource has targeted the same markets in

order to (1) provide healthcare services to employers at low cost and (2) leverage NovaSource's status as a major employer in strengthening NovaCare's relationships with local payors and healthcare providers.
